Notice to Norwood Veterans: Holiday Food Distribution Program 🇺🇸
Norwood Veteran Services has partnered with regional organizers to inform eligible residents of the Crocetti’s Turkey & Ham Giveaway scheduled for Sunday, November 22, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 1:00 PM.
Veterans may participate in one of two ways:
Direct Attendance: Attend in person at Crocetti’s in East Bridgewater during the distribution hours. Valid proof of veteran status is required at pickup.
Municipal Coordination: Veterans who face transportation or scheduling barriers may register with the Norwood Veteran Services Office. Director Derek Wennerstrand will coordinate retrieval on behalf of registered Norwood veterans.
To register for municipal pickup coordination or to request additional information, please contact the Norwood Veteran Services Office at (781) 762-1240 prior to the event date.

10-16-2026 Attention Norwood Residents:
The MWRA is taking public comments until October 30 regarding proposed Combined Sewer Overflow (CSO) control plans, and our local water/sewer rates are on the line. While we support regional environmental goals, forcing Norwood ratepayers to absorb tens of millions of dollars for legacy sewer systems in other communities is fundamentally unfair. Norwood has its own separate sewer system and urgent local infrastructure to fund.
Take action before October 30! Copy and paste the text below into the MWRA public comment portal to make your voice heard:
I oppose the $1.3 billion CSO plan from MWRA, Somerville, Cambridge. The financial burden on the Norwood MWRA ratepayers is unfair. Debt service from the project costs $36 million in MWRA assessments to Norwood ratepayers ($109 million for the $7 billion plan advocated by some). We have our own water/wastewater projects that need capital investment. We have a stormwater infrastructure to improve. We don't get funding from MWRA to finance those projects. This is not a responsible solution.
Documents, including a new letter from the Board of Selectmen, can be found on the Town's website: https://www.norwoodma.gov/government/committees_boards/board_of_selectmen/mwra_cso_plan.php
Visit https://voice.somervillema.gov/joint-cso-planning for additional details.
#NorwoodMA #NorwoodMass #NorwoodMACommunity

09.24.2026 A message from the Mass DOT:
Advisory: Norwood Roadwork on Route 1 between the Walpole and Westwood Town Lines
Nightly, Sunday through Thursday, beginning Sunday, September 27, through Thursday, November 5, from 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. the following morning.
NORWOOD - The Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT) is announcing that it will be performing roadwork on Route 1 northbound and southbound between the Walpole and Westwood town lines in Norwood. Nightly work is scheduled Sunday through Thursday from 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. the following morning, beginning Sunday, September 27, through Thursday, November 5. Work is anticipated to be completed by Friday morning, November 6.
Lane closures on Route 1 northbound and southbound will be in place. Temporary traffic alterations, including lane and shoulder closures, will occur as needed. At least one lane of travel will be maintained at all times, and police will assist with traffic control and safety setups.
Appropriate signage and messaging will be in place to guide drivers through the work area.
Drivers traveling through the affected area should expect delays, reduce speed, and use caution.
All scheduled work is weather dependent and subject to change without notice.
#NorwoodMA #NorwoodMass #NorwoodMACommunity #MassDot

September 23, 2026
🚨Protect your water bill 🚨
The Town of Norwood is encouraging residents to review and submit public comments regarding the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority’s (MWRA) proposed $1.3 Billion Draft Updated Combined Sewer Overflow (CSO) Control Plan.
While this regional infrastructure initiative aims to address CSO discharges in the Cambridge, Somerville, and surrounding watershed areas, the current proposal shifts 60% of the project’s total cost to the broader MWRA regional system.
Under this regional cost-allocation model, Norwood ratepayers would be responsible for an estimated $35 million+ in long-term debt service, despite receiving no direct local infrastructure improvements.
The Norwood Board of Selectmen has formally submitted comments advocating for a re-evaluation of the funding allocation and a review of lower-cost alternative plans. We encourage you to submit comments.
The CSO updated plan (as well as additional informative documents) can be found on the Town of Norwood website on the Selectmen’s page: https://www.norwoodma.gov/government/committees_boards/board_of_selectmen/mwra_cso_plan.php
Public Comment Deadline: October 30, 2026
Submit Comments by Email: Comments can be emailed to the project team at UpdatedCSOControlPlan@aecom.com
Submit Comments in the Online Comment Portal: Comments can be submitted to the project team electronically using the online comment portal hosted by Plan Engage at: https://us.planengage.com/updatedcsocontrolplan/page/home
Submit Comments by Public Hearing:
September 24, 2026 1pm-3pm (Virtual) register for the virtual meeting at: https://cbi-org.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_iki7BcLZQfiCFu6UsmwuqQ#/registration
October 28, 2026 6pm-8pm (Virtual or In-Person) Attend in person at Somerville City Hall Council Chambers, 93 Highland Ave., Somerville, MA Or register for the virtual meeting at: https://cbi-org.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_T84wgkwMSeiCzLAOBdq16g
